column1: # html-decision-v1-gold-v2 gold labels of html-decision-v1 (Issue #152), read only by the scorer. Rebuilt from html-decision-v1-gold and the independent adjudication html-decision-v1-adjudication (sha256 ff8cd6db6e50e0b9169acf2749122416384e6f3e2d5cfaa2cdfc519bf4563cc7).
# Same columns and syntax as gold.tsv; reviewer is the independent adjudicator. Any change is a new gold version with a new frozen hash.

# changelog: case:embed-ambiguous-01 expected (gpt-6.1-sol): The stated integrateWithPage=yes constraint requires the content to join the current document. Unknown source-document status does not override that explicit requirement.

# changelog: case:embed-ambiguous-01 acceptable (gpt-6.1-sol): The corpus says content sharing styles, layout and the accessibility tree must become part of the current document, for example inside a div.
# changelog: case:embed-ambiguous-01 ineligible (gpt-6.1-sol): The corpus describes iframe as isolated from the parent styles, which conflicts with the explicit integration constraint.

# changelog: case:embed-ambiguous-01 rationale (gpt-6.1-sol): The original rationale treats source-document status as decisive while ignoring a mandatory integration requirement already supplied by the case.

# changelog: case:embed-ambiguous-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): The original spans distinguish grouping from embedding but omit the passage establishing how to meet the explicit integration constraint.

# changelog: case:embed-help-01 expected (gpt-6.1-sol): The requirement says the articles must share styles and the accessibility tree. The corpus explicitly allows copying another document's markup into the current document to achieve this.
# changelog: case:embed-help-01 acceptable (gpt-6.1-sol): Separate source documents can supply markup integrated into a div; the requirement does not insist on retaining a separate browsing context.
# changelog: case:embed-help-01 ineligible (gpt-6.1-sol): An iframe preserves isolation rather than the required shared styles and accessibility tree.
# changelog: case:embed-help-01 assumptions (gpt-6.1-sol): The case specifies that integration is mandatory, so isolation-preferred is not a permissible unstated priority.

# changelog: case:embed-help-01 rationale (gpt-6.1-sol): Being authored as a separate document does not require remaining isolated at display time. The original conditional label relaxes a stated must without authorization.
# changelog: case:embed-help-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): Retain the directly relevant isolation and integration passages and add the div grouping definition supporting the selected candidate.
# changelog: case:embed-video-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): Add the isolation passage because isolation from parent styles is an explicit requirement and a premise of the rationale.
# changelog: case:embed-widget-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): The added isolation sentence directly supports the requirement that the partner page's styles stay separate.
# changelog: case:script-csp-01 acceptable (gpt-6.1-sol): Both choices load a permitted same-origin classic script. runAfterParse=no means delayed execution is not required; it does not prohibit it.

# changelog: case:script-csp-01 ineligible (gpt-6.1-sol): Plain inline code is blocked and defer does not cure inline CSP restrictions. A module is not guaranteed to preserve the specified classic-script semantics; external+defer violates no stated constraint.

# changelog: case:script-csp-01 rationale (gpt-6.1-sol): The absence of a requirement to defer does not make deferral incorrect. The rationale should distinguish an unconditional external solution from a nonce-dependent one.

# changelog: case:script-csp-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): These focused passages support the permitted external choices, the conditional nonce alternative, and the lack of guaranteed classic-to-module equivalence without unrelated event-handler detail.

# changelog: case:script-csp-inline-01 assumptions (gpt-6.1-sol): A hash can authorize a block by a different mechanism, but hash availability alone does not authorize the candidate named inline+nonce. The nonce on the block must be authorized by the policy.

# changelog: case:script-csp-inline-01 rationale (gpt-6.1-sol): The current policy has no nonce authorization, and adding a nonce attribute alone cannot satisfy it. Hash authorization is a separate mechanism not named by this candidate.

# changelog: case:script-csp-inline-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): These exact excerpts establish the inline restriction and the possible specific-block exception without the unrelated event-handler discussion.

# changelog: case:script-defer-external-01 ineligible (gpt-6.1-sol): An ordinary external classic script in the head runs while parsing rather than only after the whole document is parsed. The original list omits this directly conflicting candidate.

# changelog: case:script-defer-external-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): Add the default classic-script behavior to justify rejecting a head script with src but without defer, while retaining evidence for the required scheduling.

# changelog: case:script-defer-inline-01 ineligible (gpt-6.1-sol): Both external candidates require the file that the case explicitly disallows; plain inline, inline defer and a nonce do not provide the required scheduling.

# changelog: case:script-defer-inline-01 rationale (gpt-6.1-sol): The corpus supports this candidate-level conditional answer, but it does not justify a universal claim about every possible way to delay JavaScript.

# changelog: case:script-module-01 ineligible (gpt-6.1-sol): The distinct external candidate describes a classic src script, not type=module; it does not express the required module-loading mode any more than the other classic candidates do.
# changelog: case:script-module-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): Add the exact module-loading definition to support rejecting classic loading modes as well as explaining default deferral.

# changelog: case:script-shared-01 acceptable (gpt-6.1-sol): The requirement does not mandate a shared file, a caching policy, or immediate execution. Inline repetition still works, and after-parse external execution is permitted; external remains the preferable reusable form.

# changelog: case:script-shared-01 ineligible (gpt-6.1-sol): A module can change the specified classic-code semantics. Inline+defer and inline+nonce add unnecessary attributes here but the corpus does not establish that they violate a requirement, so leave them unclassified.
# changelog: case:script-shared-01 rationale (gpt-6.1-sol): The corpus describes the benefit of external reuse rather than a prohibition on repeated inline code or optional deferral.

# changelog: case:script-shared-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): These passages support both classic inclusion forms, the reuse preference, permitted deferred timing, and the difference between ignored inline defer and a potentially incompatible module conversion.

# changelog: case:script-snippet-01 acceptable (gpt-6.1-sol): No immediate-execution requirement is stated, so a deferred external classic script also meets the constraints. Being short and used on one page does not prohibit an external file.

# changelog: case:script-snippet-01 ineligible (gpt-6.1-sol): Module execution can change classic-script scope and strictness. Inline+defer is ignored and a nonce is unnecessary without CSP, but neither is shown to violate this case; leave those candidates unclassified.

# changelog: case:script-snippet-01 rationale (gpt-6.1-sol): The original rationale incorrectly rules out caching merely because only one page uses the file and does not account for harmless optional deferral.

# changelog: case:script-snippet-01 evidenceSpans (gpt-6.1-sol): Add direct support for optional external deferral, the ineffectiveness of inline defer, and the semantic risk of changing classic code into a module.

case:embed-card-01
column7: The card is part of the current document and is styled with it, so div groups it; iframe would load a separate document with its own browsing context, which this content is not.

column1: case:embed-widget-01
column7: The booking page is a separate document whose styles must stay apart, so iframe embeds it in its own browsing context; div cannot hold another document. It needs no device feature, so no allow permission should be granted.

column1: case:embed-help-01
column7: The articles originate as separate HTML documents, but they must share the current page's styles, layout and accessibility tree. Copy their markup into the current document in a div as described by the corpus; iframe isolation would violate that explicit integration requirement.

column1: case:embed-video-01
column7: The call page is a separate, isolated document, so iframe; it needs the camera, so allow should list exactly that requested feature and nothing more.

column1: case:embed-ambiguous-01
column7: The content must share the page's styles, layout and accessibility tree, so integrate its markup into the current document in a div. Whether its source is a separate HTML document does not change this requirement; an iframe would keep it isolated.

column1: case:list-install-01
column7: The steps must be done in order, and ol is for items whose order matters.

column1: case:list-ingredients-01
column7: The ingredients can be gathered in any order, and ul is for items whose order does not matter.

column1: case:list-ranking-01
column7: The position of each book is its rank, so the order carries meaning and ol fits.

column1: case:list-nav-01
column7: The footer links have no meaningful order, so ul fits.

column1: case:list-ambiguous-01
column7: Nothing says whether the order of the party items matters, which is exactly what separates ol from ul; the right move is to ask.

column1: case:script-snippet-01
column7: A short classic script used on one page can be included inline or in an external file; external+defer is also acceptable because immediate execution is not required. Cross-page reuse is absent, but an external file can still be cached; redundant inline attributes do not create a requirement violation.

column1: case:script-shared-01
column7: Prefer an external file because every page can reuse and cache it, but inline repetition also satisfies the stated requirement. external+defer is also acceptable because immediate execution is not required; unnecessary inline attributes are not evidence of an incorrect solution.

column1: case:script-csp-01
column7: Use a same-origin external classic script allowed by script-src self. external+defer is also acceptable because no immediate-execution requirement is stated; plain inline code remains blocked, and a nonce-authorized inline alternative would require an additional policy assumption.

column1: case:script-csp-inline-01
column7: Among the listed candidates, use an inline classic script with a nonce only if the CSP can be changed to authorize that matching nonce. The current self-only policy blocks inline code, so if that authorization is unavailable none of the listed choices meets all constraints.

column1: case:script-defer-external-01
column7: defer runs an external classic script after parsing in document order; on an inline classic script defer is ignored, and the code is not a module.

column1: case:script-defer-inline-01
column7: Among the listed candidates, an inline module supplies after-parse execution without adding a file, conditional on the classic code being compatible with module semantics. defer has no effect on an inline classic script; if module conversion is unsuitable, none of the listed choices meets all constraints.

column1: case:script-module-01
column7: Module scripts are already deferred by default, so defer is not needed and has no effect; the code imports modules, so it must be loaded as a module.
